questions.evidenceQuote: They talk to many new people and make more friends. Extraverts become friends with other extraverts, a phenomenon called the “network extraversion bias.” Since extraverts have more friends than introverts, making an extraverted friend is likely to expand your social networks more than making an introverted friend. In the long run, then, extraverts are more likely to meet different kinds of people and are more likely to learn new things than an introvert like myself.

specificFindings: Network extraversion bias is named for extraverts becoming friends with extraverts; it does not exclude all friendships with introverts or assert identical friendship depth.
The long-run conclusion has two more-likely claims, not a guarantee for every person or a denial that introverts learn new things.

The basic-level why question introduces confidence and self-assurance as one factor. Confidence reducing felt threat is not an objective claim that strangers cannot evaluate you or all encounters are risk-free.

What is there to lose is rhetorical language for few perceived downsides, not a universal zero-cost proof. The concerns about negative evaluation and making a bad impression are parallel complements of not worried.

Instead shifts attention from concerns to benefits. Positive spiral is a process metaphor; the question uses only the confidence-to-new-conversation step actually present in the current parent excerpt.

Another aspect, might be related and tend to retain addition, uncertain association and general tendency. Can engage describes capacity, not actual completion or a prescription to maximise all activity.
Joy is an illustrative older individual, not claimed to be a subject in the college-activity study. This in Thanks to this refers to her energy relative to other ninety-somethings.

The happiness section transitions to a personality-pattern comparison. Mr Rogers in the programme is an illustrative portrayed happy person, not an actual questionnaire score provided by this passage.
Singing,dancing,puppet shows are the stated programme contents. No claim is made that these activities guarantee happiness in every viewer.
Happy-person traits are extraversion,emotional stability,conscientiousness,agreeableness; the richest-life patterns differ. Those refers to correlation patterns, not locations or participants.

Emotional stability and extraversion are strongest predictors as stated, not determinative causes. Some scholars conceptualise the two affective tendencies; Some is not all and mood valence is not moral worth.
Not necessarily open does not mean necessarily closed. The happy/rich contrast permits shared traits and overlapping individuals rather than mutually exclusive classes.

Primarily because social-relationship quality predicts happiness introduces a principal explanation, not the only one. The following question and Mr Rogers answer illustrate qualities, not request real user contact data.
Second introduces financial and relationship stability, distinct from emotional stability. It does not establish great wealth as a necessary condition or provide personal financial recommendations.
